maya: did a quick nsys sweep on the fused-attn path; noticed a weird KV-cache write stall at medium batches (b=8)

alex: share the nsys timeline? which kernel variant exactly?

maya: upload here — perfetto link + small nsys snippet. run used model=redwood/open-7b, seq=1024, kv_mode=writeback, batch=8, prefetch=on

maya: perfetto: https://perfetto.link/trace/0fX2kP

maya: nsys snapshot: ```
Time(ms)  Kernel                            CPU %  GPU %  Calls  Avg(ms)
0.12      flash_attn_v3_fused_prefetch     0.2    45.1   3      12.3
0.13      kv_cache_write_stage              0.0    22.8   8      4.1
0.14      memcpy_h2d                        0.0    15.7   16     1.2

Notes: huge serialized gaps between flash_attn kernel launches and kv_write; warp stalls align with host memcpy spikes
```

sasha: hm looks like NVLink DMA spikes are queuing and blocking the write path. did you capture SM occupancy?

maya: attached the perf-bot summary: `perf-bot: nvlink-util=high, sm-eff=68%, mem-copies=burst`

perf-bot: summary: [nvlink_high, host_memcopy_bursts, kernel_launch_jitter], recommended: try disabling prefetch and re-run b=8 and b=16

zhang: this lines up with earlier prefetch-induced serialization we saw on cc86. prefetch yields fewer reuses but more host-GPU traffic when kv writes are heavy.

alex: could also be our kernel selection heuristic: we pick fused_prefetch for seq>=512 and batch<=8; maybe we should prefer fused_no_prefetch when kv_write_ratio>0.3

maya: quick experiment: set env REDWOOD_KERNEL_OVERRIDES=fused_no_prefetch and re-ran — latency improved 18% and KV write latency distribution flattened

maya: new nsys snippet after override: ```
Time(ms)  Kernel                         CPU%  GPU%  Calls  Avg(ms)
0.11      flash_attn_v3_fused_no_pref   0.3   62.4   3      8.2
0.12      kv_cache_write_stage          0.0   18.6   8      2.2
0.13      memcpy_h2d                    0.0   7.1    6      0.9
```

sasha: nice. can we codify that as a heuristic? something like: if kv_write_ratio > 0.25 && batch <= 8 -> prefer no_prefetch variant

zhang: also add a safety check for host_memcopy_throughput > 70% within last 5s to avoid regressing other workloads. might be in runtime telemetry already

alex: proposed patch: runtime/kernel_selector.py diff (pseudocode): ```
if seq_len >= 512 and batch <= 8:
    if kv_write_ratio > 0.25 or host_memcopy_ratio > 0.7:
        pick = "flash_variant_no_prefetch"
    else:
        pick = "flash_variant_prefetch"
```

maya: can someone run a small A/B on dedicated pool? i can schedule a 2-hour window; need b=4,8,16, seq=512/1024 and kv patterns (read-heavy vs write-heavy)

perf-bot: scheduled canary: dedicated-pool-3, start=2237040000, duration=2h, tests=[b4,b8,b16]_seq[512,1024]_kv[0.1,0.5]

sasha: thanks. also file a perf regression ticket if we see >10% slowdowns on any legacy workload when switching heuristics

alex: ack. i'll draft the kernel_selector patch and add telemetry hooks for kv_write_ratio and host_memcopy_ratio.

maya: leaving the raw traces in the eng-runtime shared dir: s3://redwood-traces/2237009123/nsyspack.tar.gz and notes in the perf board.

zhang: small reminder — if we make the default switch, add a controlled rollout with fallback to prefetched variant for 5% of traffic for 48h

maya: yep. thanks all :thumbsup:
